new.title: Walk the 11,500-year-old T-pillars of Göbeklitepe
new.desc: Göbeklitepe on the Germuş ridge is the world's oldest known monumental temple complex, built by hunter-gatherers around 9500 BC and brought to light by Klaus Schmidt's team from 1995. Its carved T-shaped pillars show foxes, boars, snakes and birds. It joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018, and a roofed walkway runs above the enclosures.
new.tip: Go early or late to avoid the heat and tour groups; allow about 90 minutes with the visitor centre and its short film. A newly opened excavation area may need a separate route, so check the Ministry ticket page.

new.title: Descend into the Neolithic rooms of Karahantepe
new.desc: Karahantepe is a Taş Tepeler site of the 10th millennium BC, known for a rock-cut communal building with carved pillars and a cluster of human-headed statues. It lies on a rocky plateau near Yağmurlu village, east of Şanlıurfa. A protective roof and a visitor route were added so the public can walk the site.
new.tip: Take a car or a Taş Tepeler tour from Şanlıurfa (about an hour each way) and bring water and a hat; there is little shade. Check with the Şanlıurfa tourism office first, because the visitor route opened only recently.

new.title: Explore the moon-cult sanctuaries of Soğmatar
new.desc: Soğmatar (Sumatar Harabesi) in the Tektek Mountains was a centre of the moon-god Sin cult of the Harran region in Roman times, with rock-cut reliefs, tombs and a cistern complex. Inscriptions show its sanctuaries were in use from about the 2nd century AD. Local tradition links the wells and caves to the prophet Moses.
new.tip: It sits near Yağmurlu village on the same route as Karahantepe, so combine the two on a day trip. Wear sturdy shoes; paths cross bare rock.
new.q: Soğmatar Antik Kenti, Yağmurlu, Siverek, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Climb down into the rock-cut rooms of Şuayb City
new.desc: Şuayb City is a Roman-era settlement carved into soft limestone, with underground rooms, heavy lintels and a mosque built on a spot said to be the home of the prophet Shuayb (Jethro). Stone from the nearby Bazda quarries was used for Harran and other local buildings. It is among the most remote sites of the Harran plain.
new.tip: Bring a torch and sturdy shoes for the underground chambers. It is far from Harran, so go with a driver or tour and carry water.

new.title: Stop at the Ayyubid caravanserai of Han el-Ba'rur
new.desc: Han el-Ba'rur is a restored caravanserai in Göktaş village with an entrance inscription dated 1128-1129 that credits a certain Hac Hüsameddin Ali Bey. It served traders crossing the Harran plain. It lies on the road to Şuayb City and Soğmatar.
new.tip: Visit it on the loop between Harran and Şuayb City; check locally whether the planned museum fit-out is open. There is little shade, so go in the morning.

new.title: Step inside a mud-brick beehive house at Harran Kültür Evi
new.desc: The conical mud-brick houses of Harran are about 150 to 200 years old and were built with bricks taken from the ancient ruins; they stay cool in the summer heat. Harran Kültür Evi is a restored example that serves as a small museum and café, with a courtyard that offers tea and cold drinks.
new.tip: Visit in the cool morning; the courtyard café is a good tea stop. Walk the village lanes afterwards to see unrestored beehive houses.

new.title: See the Ulu Cami and university ruins of ancient Harran
new.desc: The Great Mosque of Harran dates to the mid-8th century under the Umayyad caliph Marwan II and is among the oldest in Anatolia, with a surviving square minaret. Beside it lie the ruins of the Islamic-era school often called the first university. Harran was also the centre of the Sabian moon cult.
new.tip: Go before midday as the site is unshaded; the castle next door has been closed for restoration, so view it from outside.

new.title: Wander Eski Halfeti's stone houses and look for black roses
new.desc: Eski Halfeti is the part of Halfeti on the Euphrates that was partly flooded when the Birecik Dam closed in 2000. Its stone houses and minarets rise from the reservoir, and local gardens are known for a dark crimson rose sold as the black rose. Boat trips depart from the waterfront below the old houses.
new.tip: Roses bloom mainly in spring and autumn. Walk up through the old lanes and stop at a waterfront café.

new.title: Meet the northern bald ibis at the Birecik breeding station
new.desc: The Birecik Kelaynak Breeding Station on the Euphrates keeps one of the last Turkish colonies of the northern bald ibis. It was set up in the 1970s and now holds hundreds of birds, and young are released each year to migrate.
new.tip: Late winter and spring are best, when birds are at the cliff nest sites. Entrance is cheap and the station is close to the town centre.

new.title: Climb Birecik Castle above the Euphrates
new.desc: Birecik Castle stands on a limestone hill over the Euphrates and the town. Sources date it variously to the Byzantine era or the 13th-century Artuqid period, and its stone came from the Kalazan Dağı quarries. The hill gives a view of the river and the bridge.
new.tip: Go near sunset for the view of the river. Access conditions vary, so check locally.

new.title: Look over Siverek from its old castle mound
new.desc: Siverek Castle sits on a high artificial mound in the town and is thought to go back to the Assyrian period. Siverek was long a trading town between Urfa and Diyarbakır, and the castle is a local landmark among its few historic sites.
new.tip: Check access locally, as part of the site may be fenced. Pair it with a meal in the town centre.

new.title: Take in the Atatürk Dam, the Euphrates' giant reservoir
new.desc: The Atatürk Dam near Bozova is a rock-fill dam on the Euphrates, completed in 1990 as the centrepiece of the GAP project. Its reservoir is Türkiye's third largest and feeds the Şanlıurfa irrigation tunnels.
new.tip: Access to the dam crest depends on security; stop at viewpoints along the road and picnic spots by the lake.

new.title: Watch the sun rise behind the gods of Mount Nemrut
new.desc: Around 62 BC King Antiochus I of Commagene built a tomb-sanctuary on Nemrut's 2,134 m summit, with colossal seated statues of himself and Greek-Persian gods, now headless. A 49 m tumulus of loose stone rises behind them. UNESCO listed the site in 1987 and the statues survived the 2023 earthquakes.
new.tip: The summit road is open roughly April to October; dress warmly for dawn. Organised sunrise trips run from Kahta and Adıyaman, and the last stretch is on foot.
new.q: Nemrut Dağı Milli Parkı, Kahta, Adıyaman

new.title: Cross the Roman Cendere Bridge near Kahta
new.desc: The Cendere (Severan) Bridge was built under Septimius Severus around AD 200 over the Cendere stream. Its 34 m main arch makes it one of the best preserved Roman bridges in Turkey. It still carries traffic and came through the 2023 earthquake undamaged.
new.tip: Combine it with Karakuş and Nemrut on one day. It is free and takes 15 minutes.

new.title: See the Commagene queens' column at Karakuş Tumulus
new.desc: Karakuş Tumulus was built around 30 to 20 BC by Mithridates II of Commagene for Queen Isias and princesses Antiochis and Aka. Doric columns topped with an eagle, a lion and a bull ring the mound. The eagle column fell in the 2023 earthquake and was restored, and the site is open again.
new.tip: It stands by the road on the Kahta-Nemrut route, so it is a quick stop.

new.title: Visit the restored Eski Kahta Castle
new.desc: Eski Kahta Castle (also called Yeni Kale) is a medieval fortress on a cliff above the Kahta stream. Restoration ended after the site had been shut for about 17 years, and it reopened to visitors. It sits near the village of Kocahisar, close to Arsameia.
new.tip: Opening hours vary; ask in Kocahisar if the gate is shut.
new.q: Eski Kahta Kalesi, Kocahisar, Kahta, Adıyaman

new.title: Discover the Roman rock tombs of Perre
new.desc: Perre (Pirin) was a city of Commagene and later a Roman and Byzantine centre, with rock-cut tombs and a Roman fountain. Excavations in 2025 produced new Roman-era finds, and a holographic exhibit was introduced for visitors. The site sits near Pirin village on the Adıyaman-Kahta road.
new.tip: Check the Adıyaman Museum's published visiting hours first; dig seasons may restrict areas.
new.q: Perre Antik Kenti, Pirin, Adıyaman Merkez, Adıyaman

new.title: Take the Euphrates boat trip to Savaşan and Rumkale
new.desc: Boats leave Eski Halfeti on the Birecik Dam reservoir for the half-submerged village of Savaşan, where a mosque of 1844 stands in the water. Longer trips continue to the ruins of Rumkale. The ride shows the drowned old town from the water.
new.tip: Agree price and route before boarding; the full trip to Rumkale is about an hour each way.

new.title: Cruise the Kızılin Canyon where the Göksu meets the Euphrates
new.desc: Kızılin Canyon in Besni is cut into the Euphrates banks at the confluence with the Göksu and has about 300 registered caves over some 200 hectares. A boat pier was installed for river tours, and traces of settlement go back thousands of years.
new.tip: Boat availability is seasonal, so ask at the pier. It is a long drive from Besni, so budget half a day.

new.title: Ski the volcanic slopes of Karacadağ
new.desc: Karacadağ is an extinct volcano and its ski centre at about 1,900 m draws well over 100,000 mostly local visitors each winter. The slopes lie above the Siverek plateau near the Diyarbakır and Mardin borders.
new.tip: Winter only; lodging has at times been closed for renovation, so confirm before travelling.

new.title: Eat hand-kneaded Adıyaman çiğ köfte at Esensoy
new.desc: Esensoy Çiğ Köfte, on Buhara Caddesi, is cited by local guides as a first stop for Adıyaman's raw-meat çiğ köfte, kneaded by hand on a marble counter since 1983. Adıyaman's version is a signature dish of the city.
new.tip: Order it with ayran or şalgam, wrapped in lettuce.
new.q: Esensoy Çiğ Köfte, Buhara Caddesi, Yenipınar, Adıyaman

new.title: Eat trout beside Atatürk Dam lake at Neşet'in Yeri
new.desc: Neşet'in Yeri is a lakeside restaurant near Kahta that Fodor's recommends for its vine-shaded outdoor seating. The kitchen is known for trout and kebabs, and it is a relaxed spot after Mount Nemrut.
new.tip: Order the fish; check that it is open in low season.
new.q: Neşet'in Yeri, Atatürk Barajı, Kahta, Adıyaman

new.title: Dine on a floating restaurant at Başkanın Yeri Duba
new.desc: Halfeti Başkanın Yeri Duba Restaurant is a family-run floating restaurant on the Euphrates reservoir, serving river fish and Halfeti kebab with eggplant.
new.tip: Try the şabut or patlıcanlı Halfeti kebabı; check water levels first.
new.q: Halfeti Başkanın Yeri Duba Restaurant, Köse Sokak, Şimaliye, Halfeti, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Eat a Birecik lunch at Kalealtı Gülbaba Lokantası
new.desc: Kalealtı Gülbaba Lokantası is a local lokanta listed among Birecik's restaurants, below the castle hill. Birecik is known for nohut dürümü and eggplant kebab.
new.tip: Try nohut dürümü or patlıcan kebabı.

new.title: Have breakfast above the Euphrates at Seyr-i Fırat
new.desc: Seyr-i Fırat Cafe & Kahvaltı is a Birecik café on the river, serving Turkish breakfast with a view of the Euphrates and the bridge.
new.tip: Go at sunset or for breakfast; the bridge is lit in the evening.
new.q: Seyr-i Fırat Cafe & Kahvaltı, Birecik, Şanlıurfa
